stemMd: A box is chosen at random from two boxes. One contains 2 gold and 1 silver token; the other contains 1 gold and 3 silver tokens. A drawn token is gold. What is the probability the first box was chosen?
explanationMd: The gold contributions are $(1/2)(2/3)=1/3$ and $(1/2)(1/4)=1/8$. Divide the first by their sum: $(1/3)/(11/24)=8/11$.

distractorRationale.b: Uses likelihood without updating the box probability.
distractorRationale.a: Keeps the prior despite informative evidence.
distractorRationale.d: Counts gold tokens across boxes as though each token were equally sampled.
